title: Pesco 4E Advances Technologies For Future European Combat Ships
text:
PESCO 4E advances technologies for future European Combat Ships

Under the leadership of the Spanish Navy and the European Defence Agency (EDA), the 6th international workshop of the PESCO Essential Elements of European Escort (4E) project was held in Ferrol, Spain, from 28–30 April, with the support of Navantia at the COEX facility.

Developed within the framework of the EU Permanent Structured Cooperation (PESCO) PESCO 4E is managed as an EDA Category B programme, a mechanism that allows groups of member states to jointly develop military capabilities on a voluntary basis. The countries involved in the initiative include Spain, Greece, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, and Sweden, while Germany contributes as an observer.

The workshop advanced on the requirements for five critical systems expected to equip the next generation of European naval combat ships: counter-unmanned vehicle defence, satellite-independent positioning, autonomous navigation, directed-energy weapons, and multipurpose unmanned surface systems.

PESCO 4E is laying the foundations for Europe’s future smart naval combat ships: digitally integrated, interconnected through a true “system of systems,” and designed to reduce fragmentation across the European maritime capability landscape while reinforcing strategic autonomy and Europe’s defence technological and industrial base.

The event gathered 59 participants from 24 companies, alongside representatives from EDA, the Spanish Navy, and the Ministries of Defence of Portugal, Italy, Greece, the Netherlands, Germany, Sweden, and Spain.

The project aims to strengthen European naval capabilities through the development of interoperable, modular, and resilient systems for future warships and also leverages the European Defence Fund (EDF) programmes to support associated industrial research and development activities.

The workshop highlighted the strong commitment of both ministries of defence and industry partners to advancing Europe’s naval future through enhanced cooperation and innovation.
